original_blog_post.title: LLMs are eroding my software engineering career and I don't know what to do
original_blog_post.context: Anonymous senior engineer with 10 years experience in finance/payments, published the post that gained 1000+ upvotes and comments on Hacker News within 24 hours

hacker_news_thread.title: LLMs are eroding my software engineering career and I don't know what to do
hacker_news_thread.stats: 1129 points, 1064 comments at time of research

xu_paper.title: AI-Assisted Programming May Decrease the Productivity of Experienced Developers
xu_paper.finding: Found experienced developers showed a 19% drop in original code output after Copilot adoption
xu_paper.methodology: Observational study of open-source repositories before and after Copilot adoption

metr_2025.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
metr_2025.finding: 19% longer task completion time when using AI tools
metr_2025.perception: Developers felt 20% faster despite taking 19% longer
metr_2025.methodology: 16 experienced OS developers, 246 real issues, randomized AI/no-AI conditions

metr_2026.title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
metr_2026.finding: Estimated 18% speedup for original developers, but confidence interval from -38% to +9%
metr_2026.methodology: Follow-up to 2025 study with selection bias acknowledged
metr_2026.note: Authors acknowledge selection effects make the data unreliable, but believe speedup is likely occurring

opsera_2026.title: 2026 AI Coding Impact Benchmark Report
opsera_2026.finding: AI-generated pull requests wait 4.6 times longer for review than human-written code
opsera_2026.context: Reflects trust deficit and governance challenges in AI code review

ibm_watsonx_study.title: Examining the Use and Impact of an AI Code Assistant on Developer Productivity and Experience in the Enterprise
ibm_watsonx_study.methodology: Surveys of 669 developers + 15 unmoderated usability tests
ibm_watsonx_study.finding: Productivity gains exist but distribute unevenly - junior developers benefit more while senior engineers absorb review debt

verification_summary.notes: All primary sources verified. METR follow-up study acknowledges methodological limitations but provides valuable context about selection bias in AI productivity research.
